o.text: Ultimately from Proto-Turkic *kem (“who”). Cognate with Turkish kim, Old Turkic 𐰚𐰢 (kem, “who”), etc.
From Proto-Turkic *adut. Cognate with Turkish avuç, Chuvash ывӑҫ (yvăś).
From Arabic عَيْب (ʕayb). Though can be considered as alternative forms, today the flaw sense in eyib and, shame sense in ayıb is more strong in colloquial speech.
